## c9db537b5068

**Domain question; no reproduced defect inside the declared generator domain.** The generator intentionally requires the rectangle marker bounding box to have at least one background row and column on every side. A rival can therefore say “fill the rectangle only when all four margins are positive; otherwise return the input unchanged.” It matches all 3,200 generated samples checked across four difficulty settings; none touched a border, and all passed the task validator (`checks/audit/c9db537b5068/scan_summary.json`).

The broader canonical Racket semantics do handle border-touching rectangles. The exact 6×8 top-border witness in `checks/audit/c9db537b5068/witness.json` is filled by canonical Racket (rule hash `3ae37aff2b7c`) while the margin-gated rival leaves it unchanged. The generator’s `self_check` rejects that witness with `bbox must have at least one background row/column on every side`, so it is outside the documented generator domain.

**Decision needed.** If the intended training domain is deliberately strict-interior rectangles, no issue was found. If the generator is meant to teach the full canonical rule, relax the margin restriction and add border-touching examples so the margin-gated shortcut is refuted.
